subject: FinSage: TTFT targets and streaming chunk cadence — acceptance workstream
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 20:05:00 -0700
Subject: FinSage: TTFT targets and streaming chunk cadence — acceptance workstream

Hi Samir — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick post-call recap and concrete asks so we can align on the pilot/probe: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct if I misstate anything):
- Primary KPIs: user-facing Time-to-first-token (TTFT) and steady-state throughput.
- Target TTFT: p50 ~ <120 ms; p75 < 150 ms; p95 < 350 ms (for typical 512-token prompts).
- Throughput & concurrency: expecting sustained 350–450 requests/sec, with peak concurrency ~ 60–80 simultaneous sessions.
- Streaming preference: you said you prefer WebSocket for the in-app SDK integration but are open to SSE for public endpoints; chunk cadence ideally 120–300 ms per chunk for perceived responsiveness.
- Fallbacks: mobile clients should be able to accept slightly larger chunk windows (up to 400 ms) to reduce battery/connection churn.

Asks / next steps: 
1) Can you confirm the above TTFT targets and the throughput envelope? (Approve or suggest tweaks.)
2) Share a representative load trace (CSV or flame) and 2–3 sample payloads (typical prompt lengths, system messages).
3) Approve a 1-hour probe window next Tuesday (2027-06-22) where we run synthetic traffic and a live-sample stream test.
4) Olive Security requested a short list of where we store KV/cache and whether any chunked payloads persist in logs — we can provide that once you confirm probe timing.

Attached: [Attachment: ttft_probe_spec.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)] — contains the probe plan, measurement points (TTFT p50/p95, chunk latency), and suggested payload mix.

If you’re good with the approach I’ll loop in our performance engineer and set up the probe environment on Redwood Dedicated.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>

Cc: Olive Security <security@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinSage: TTFT targets and streaming chunk cadence — acceptance workstream

Rishi — thanks for the tight summary. Confirms what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT: the p50/p75 figures look right; p95 at 350ms is acceptable for web UI but for our internal analyst desktop app we’d like a tighter p95 target if possible (ideally < 300ms) once the pilot stabilizes.
- Throughput: 350–450 req/s is realistic for our busiest workflows. For the pilot please assume a 20% spike window to validate autoscaling/fallback.
- Streaming protocol: internal desktop will prefer WebSocket (we use multiplexed channels); external endpoints (customer-facing) can be SSE. We’d like Redwood’s recommendation on whether the WebSocket vs SSE choice materially affects TTFT for our expected payload shapes.
- Chunk cadence: 100–250 ms preferred for desktop; mobile 200–400 ms. We’d also be interested in a short write-up on reassembly/ordering guarantees if chunks are delivered out of order on flaky mobile networks.

We can provide a load trace and 3 sample payloads by EOD Wednesday. Please go ahead and schedule the probe for Tue 2027-06-22 — Ben/CX please call out the exact time window.

Attached: [Attachment: finlytics_streaming_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)]

—Samir
Head of Platform Engineering | FinSage Analytics
samir@finlytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinSage: TTFT targets and streaming chunk cadence — acceptance workstream

Adding a recommended pilot runbook and a few operational checks — tagging Marissa for commercial cadence and scheduling: 

Proposed pilot approach (1-hour synthetic + sampled live):
- Environment: Dedicated pool (NVIDIA H100 x8 nodes) to remove noisy-neighbor variance.
- Synthetic load: ramp to 400 req/s baseline, include 20% spike to 480 req/s for 5 min.
- Payload mix: 60% short queries (~64 tokens), 30% medium (~256 tokens), 10% long (~1024 tokens).
- Measurement: TTFT (p50/p75/p95), chunk delivery latency (per-chunk mean, 95th), end-to-end throughput, connection drop rate.
- Canary: start with 10% of traffic hitting the new streaming config (in blue/green style) and measure TTFT delta vs baseline.

Operational notes:
- Autoscale thresholds: recommend CPU/GPU utilization target 70–80% with burst policy to add 2 nodes at sustained 90%.
- Tracing: enable request id propagation and Redwood’s distributed-trace header so FinSage can correlate traces with their telemetry.
- Fallback policy: if p95 TTFT exceeds 500 ms or chunk-drop > 2% for 5 minutes, route to a lower-quant model variant and alert.

Next steps I’ll take:
- Block the probe window for Tue 2027-06-22 09:00–10:00 PT and set up the Dedicated pool.
- Prep a small k8s manifest + traffic harness; share by EOD Thu.
- Confirm who from FinSage owns the payload/key exchange (Samir?) and whether we need a signed NDA/POA before running live-sample traffic.

Ben Carter

- Prep ask: please send the load trace and 3 sample payloads (as Rishi requested) + a test service account key (short-lived) by EOD Wed so Ben’s team can preload the harness.
